title: Interactive Digital Laboratory Database — Overview and definition
body: Signature edition. Original Signature methods, framings, and analyses developed for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout; never mixed with public-harvest records. Simulations, virtual instruments, experiments, and assessment criteria for digital labs. The Interactive Digital Laboratory Database documents laboratories without walls: interactive simulations, virtual instruments (oscilloscopes, spectrometers, microscopes — simulated faithfully), guided experiments, and the assessment criteria that prove learning happened. A good virtual lab teaches experimental thinking — hypothesis, measurement, error analysis — not just button-clicking. Each record includes the simulation model, the instrument behaviors, the experiment protocol, and what students should be able to do afterward.

title: Interactive Digital Laboratory Database — Knowledge: technical reference
body: Signature edition. Original Signature methods, framings, and analyses developed for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout; never mixed with public-harvest records. Lab anatomy: SIMULATION (the physics/math model, numerical method, fidelity statement) + INSTRUMENTS (virtual controls matching real ones; noise and limits modeled; calibration procedures included) + PROTOCOL (the experiment steps, adapted: what to vary, what to measure, how many trials) + ANALYSIS (error propagation, curve fitting, conclusion) + ASSESSMENT (rubric: technique, analysis, conclusion quality). Fidelity discipline: every lab states what is modeled, what is approximated, what is omitted — students must know the difference. Noise modeling: measurement noise teaches error analysis (without it, labs teach nothing about uncertainty). Instrument behaviors: range limits, resolution, warm-up, calibration drift — the realistic details that teach care. Assessment: performance-based (can the student DO the analysis?), not just multiple choice.

demo.title: Execution: Bayesian knowledge tracing update
demo.code: let pL=0.3;const pT=0.2,pS=0.1,pG=0.25;function update(correct){const pC=pL*(1-pS)+(1-pL)*pG;const pLgiven=correct?(pL*(1-pS)/pC):(pL*pS/(pL*pS+(1-pL)*(1-pG)));pL=pLgiven+(1-pLgiven)*pT;return pL;}const responses=[1,1,0,1,1];const traj=responses.map(update);const mastered=traj[traj.length-1]>=0.95;J({final:+traj[traj.length-1].toFixed(3),mastered});assert(traj.every(v=>v>=0&&v<=1),'bkt-range');assert(traj[traj.length-1]>0.3,'bkt-learn');

demo.title: Verification: concept graph is a DAG
demo.code: const edges=[['arith','algebra'],['algebra','deriv'],['deriv','backprop']];const nodes=[...new Set(edges.flat())];function topo(){const indeg={};nodes.forEach(n=>indeg[n]=0);edges.forEach(([a,b])=>indeg[b]++);const q=nodes.filter(n=>indeg[n]===0);const order=[];while(q.length){const n=q.shift();order.push(n);edges.filter(e=>e[0]===n).forEach(([a,b])=>{if(--indeg[b]===0)q.push(b);});}return order;}const order=topo();J({order,isDAG:order.length===nodes.length});assert(order.length===nodes.length&&order.indexOf('arith')<order.indexOf('backprop'),'dag');

body: Signature edition. Original Signature methods, framings, and analyses developed for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout; never mixed with public-harvest records. Tests: assembly test (all lab components present); fidelity test (statements complete); assessment test (rubrics measurable); session test (sample experiment produces analyzable data). Limitations: demos simulate simply; real labs need proper simulation engines; physical technique is out of scope (stated). Every lab carries its fidelity statement.
